questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “This time tomorrow, I ____ in a train to Mumbai.”
questions.why: An action in progress at a future time takes the future continuous. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “prolific”:
questions.why: Prolific = producing much (work, fruit, offspring). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “It took her weeks to ______ the fever.”
questions.why: Get over = recover from (GPSC 2026). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to bite the bullet”:
opts: to face a painful situation with courage
questions.why: 'Bite the bullet' means to endure something unpleasant bravely. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “The accused was convicted ____ murder.”
questions.why: 'Convicted of' a crime. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Change into a simple sentence: “As soon as he saw the police, he ran away.”
opts: On seeing the police, he ran away.
After see the police, he ran away.
At seeing the police, he ran away.
By seeing the police, he ran away.
questions.why: 'As soon as' is expressed as 'On + -ing'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct transformation: “He is so weak that he cannot walk.”
opts: He is so weak to walk.
He is weak enough to walk.
He is too weak to walk.
He is very weak to walk.
questions.why: 'So ... that ... not' becomes 'too ... to'. GPSC-style practice item.

opts: Under no circumstances did the patient should be left alone.
Under no circumstances the patient should be left alone.
Under no circumstances should the patient be left alone.
Under no circumstances should be left the patient alone.
questions.why: Negative phrase at the start: auxiliary + subject. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct version: “The patient was operated by Dr Rao yesterday.”
opts: The patient was operated at by Dr Rao yesterday.
The patient was operated of by Dr Rao yesterday.
The patient was operated on by Dr Rao yesterday.
The patient was operating by Dr Rao yesterday.
questions.why: The prepositional verb 'operate on' keeps its preposition in the passive. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Find the error: “The number of patients have increased this month.”
questions.why: 'The number of' is singular ('has'); 'a number of' is plural. GPSC-style practice item.
